bugs_found.detail: v1 computed LGD as 1 - (total_pymnt + recoveries - collection_recovery_fee) / funded_amnt. Verified empirically that total_pymnt = total_rec_prncp + total_rec_int + total_rec_late_fee + recoveries (100% match to the penny across all 18,281 train charged-off loans, mean absolute difference 0.00008). total_pymnt already includes recoveries, so adding recoveries again overstated recovered cash and understated LGD.
bugs_found.impact: v1 LGD (cash-basis) was 32.47%, systematically too low.
bugs_found.verification: Direct SQL comparison of total_pymnt against the sum of its components, with and without recoveries added; only the 'without' sum matched total_pymnt exactly.

bugs_found.bug: Ex-post realized net cash description was wrong
bugs_found.detail: v1 used total_pymnt - funded_amnt and described it as 'excludes recoveries'. Since total_pymnt already includes recoveries, this was actually already including them - the description, not the formula's recovery handling, was incorrect. The formula itself was still missing collection_recovery_fee as a cost.
bugs_found.impact: Mislabeling only (recoveries were already present); fee deduction missing.

bugs_found.bug: Ex-ante interest income assumed full 36-month interest with no prepayment adjustment
bugs_found.detail: v1 used interest_income = installment*36 - loan_amnt for every loan, i.e. the full scheduled interest as if every loan ran its complete term with no early payoff.
bugs_found.impact: Overstated expected income for 'good' loans by roughly 1/0.8265 = ~21%, based on the realized-vs-scheduled interest ratio measured on train Fully Paid loans (see v2 below).

v2.lgd_cash_basis_formula: 1 - clip((total_pymnt - collection_recovery_fee) / funded_amnt, 0, 1) -- used for the EV model
v2.lgd_standard_formula: 1 - clip((recoveries - collection_recovery_fee) / (funded_amnt - total_rec_prncp), 0, 1) -- reported for reference only, textbook LGD on outstanding principal at default
v2.interest_income_formula: scheduled_interest_i = installment_i * 36 - loan_amnt_i; interest_income_i = scheduled_interest_i * prepayment_ratio, where prepayment_ratio = sum(total_rec_int) / sum(scheduled_interest) over train Fully Paid loans only
v2.all_estimated_from: train (2012-2013) and validation (2014) only; applied to test (2015) exactly once, no re-tuning
v2.note: Model AUC/Gini/KS/Brier/calibration metrics from the original Test evaluation commit are UNCHANGED - only the economics formulas and the decision policy derived from them are corrected here.

v2_addendum_fixed_rate_methodology.bug: Fixed 70/80/90% approval-rate cut-offs were picked by sorting TEST's own PD distribution, not validation's.
v2_addendum_fixed_rate_methodology.detail: Each model's cut-off for a target approval rate (e.g. 80%) must be determined from validation only, then applied as a fixed PD value to test - sorting test itself to hit an exact approval rate on test is implicitly using test to set the policy, even though it looks like a harmless descriptive table.
v2_addendum_fixed_rate_methodology.fix: Cut-offs now computed once on validation (per score: LightGBM, XGBoost, scorecard, sub_grade map), then applied unchanged to test. Actual resulting test approval rate is reported alongside the target rate and will not land exactly on 70/80/90% as a result - that is expected and correct.
v2_addendum_fixed_rate_methodology.sub_grade_discreteness_note: sub_grade_map's actual_approval_rate_on_test_pct is further from its target than the other three scores (e.g. 75.57% actual vs 70% target) because sub_grade only has 35 discrete levels (A1-G5). Many loans share the exact same mapped PD, so the cut-off found on validation can only land between discrete buckets, not at an arbitrary percentile - a coarser instrument than a continuous model score, by construction.
